target_customer: Professional and collegiate sports teams, orthopedic doctors and physical therapists
problem: Athletes recover slowly from injuries and teams lack data on healing progress.
business_model: Hardware device sales (PentaVO wearable cold laser) with monitoring software

founders.name: Alexa Roeper
education: University of Waterloo, biomedical sciences (student when founding)
founders.background_notes: University of Waterloo article says an equestrian injury inspired the company.

founders.name: Daniel Choi
founders.background_notes: Named by the University of Waterloo article as the engineer who designed the hardware; the YC page lists only Roeper.

technical_complexity.rationale: A wearable class of laser device with software and an FDA clearance path is regulated hardware work, achieved by 2018.

defensibility.rationale: FDA clearance and clinical evidence raise the bar, but other laser makers sold clinic and at-home devices.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Established cold laser makers sold clinic devices; no evidence they copied the wearable form factor.

market_need_then: Sports teams spend on injury management and the founders reported that other at-home laser devices existed but lacked software and wearability; the Wearable Technologies article in November 2018 reports the move into sales after FDA approval.

branding.domain_note: Product site was pentavo.com, not the company name; the domain now shows a parked for sale page.
branding.community_and_virality: Press from University of Waterloo, Waterloo Region Record and Wearable Technologies; first pro customer was an MLB player per the university article.

brand_strength.rationale: Local press and university coverage but no sourced evidence of a brand driven community.

outcome_analysis: Penta Medical sold the FDA approved PentaVO wearable cold laser to sports teams and clinicians and had MLB, NFL and NCAA customers by late 2019. The YC directory lists it as inactive and pentavo.com is now a parked domain, but no source gives a shutdown cause or date, so no failure factors are assigned.
notes: Funding rests on databases: CB Insights and TheCompanyCheck give about 180K total, Seedtable gives 120K from one seed. The 30K July 2016 seed with Accelerator Centre rests on TheCompanyCheck alone; the other roughly 150K is unaccounted for and the second round has no date or amount. Competitor list is empty: LiteCure and Theralase appear only on undated market pages and are clinic devices. The Waterloo article (December 2019) says nothing about status afterward.
